subject: Literature
title: Loki the Trickster
description: A short lesson to help you apply Loki the Trickster.

hook.text: Loki is the Norse god who helps the gods and betrays them, often in the same story and for no clear reason.

buildup.text: He is a shapeshifter who becomes a salmon, a fly, a mare, and even gives birth to an eight-legged horse.

discovery.text: Trickster figures like Loki appear across world mythologies, from Anansi in Africa to Coyote in Native America.

twist.text: Loki's betrayal of the beloved god Baldr leads directly to Ragnarök, making his chaos world-ending.

climax.text: The trickster archetype represents the force of chaos that every culture recognizes as both creative and destructive.

punchline.text: Every mythology needs a character who breaks the rules.

quiz.question: What role do trickster figures like Loki play in mythology?
options: They are always purely evil villains
They represent chaos that is both creative and destructive
They are minor characters with no real impact
